primitives.verbatim_quote: Via the Rao-Blackwell theorem, we propose a shotmake probability model that conditions probability estimates on shot trajectory information, thereby reducing the variance of the new estimator relative to standard FG%.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in applying the Rao-Blackwell theorem to reduce variance in FG% estimation by incorporating shot trajectory data. Traditional FG% suffers from high variability due to small sample sizes, particularly for 3-pointers. By modeling each shot as a Bernoulli trial with a trajectory-conditioned probability, the authors derive a Rao-Blackwellized estimator that leverages additional information beyond binary outcomes. This leads to a more stable and accurate representation of shooting skill. The key insight is that spatial trajectory features—entry angle, shot depth, and left-right accuracy—are strong predictors of shot success. Conditioning on these reduces estimator variance without biasing the estimate. The resulting RB-FG% provides superior predictive power for future shooting metrics such as 3P% and true shooting percentage, offering a robust foundation for player evaluation and forecasting.
